comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: The ordinary Mathematics programme has a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling choices. This example includes a modelling course in differential equations. It uses restricted and further mathematics choices to build the recommended preparation in differential equations and numerical mathematics. At least 15 EC of profiling must be at level 2 or 3.
components: Restricted choice that prepares for differential-equation modelling.
Mathematics choice covering numerical methods before the modelling course.
Part of the 45 EC available for elective courses or an approved minor.
Advanced modelling after study of differential equations and numerical methods.
Includes individual mathematical research and a shared mathematics communication component.
At least 15 EC across the full profiling space must be at level 2 or 3.

core: Mathematical structures, logic, calculus, linear algebra, numerical and differential methods, probability and rigorous analysis
Programming, discrete mathematics, scientific computing, algorithms, optimisation and artificial intelligence
Probability, statistics, data analysis, stochastic modelling and empirical prediction
adjacent: Mathematics for climate, weather, Earth systems, resources and energy technology
Mathematics for economics, finance, econometrics, strategic interaction and institutional decisions
Mathematical modelling for biological and life-science systems
History and development of mathematical ideas
questions: How can mathematical structures and models explain and predict complex real-world systems?

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, algorithms & stochastic data models
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, linear algebra and probability to build models, and use programming, algorithms and numerical methods to study their behaviour. Explore applications in prediction, optimisation and robotics.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains a sustained mathematical and computational spine with concrete algorithmic and stochastic applications, while the label avoids claiming the target programme’s proof-intensive pure-mathematics depth.
progression: Python and logic precede algorithms and discrete optimisation. Calculus and linear algebra support numerical methods, linear systems and robotics. Introductory data work precedes machine learning and later neural-network models.

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling, Earth systems & scientific data
alternatives.concept: Use calculus, modelling and data analysis to study Earth systems, climate and energy. Apply geospatial methods to environmental observations and use quantitative models to investigate physical and resource systems.
alternatives.labelReason: The plan combines mathematics and modelling with geospatial methods, geology, climate and energy.
progression: Sustainability, programming and mathematical foundations precede geospatial analysis and modelling. Basic energy analysis precedes renewable-system design, while Earth system tools and geology support later soils, geochemistry and resources.
alternatives.distinctness: 12 courses differ each way from the first option, with geospatial analysis, Earth science and renewable energy.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, economics & quantitative decision models
alternatives.concept: Apply calculus, probability, statistics and computation to economic choices, markets and public policy. Use optimisation and econometrics to study decisions under constraints and estimate relationships from data.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum retains a substantial mathematics, statistics, computation and optimisation spine while adding finance, macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics and econometrics, so the label names mathematics, economics and quantitative decision models together.
progression: Economics, accounting, Python and calculus precede quantitative applications. Early data work and probability support later statistical learning and decisions under uncertainty. Public economics and microeconomics precede later econometrics and optimisation.
alternatives.distinctness: 6 and 14 courses differ each way from the first and second options respectively, with economics, finance and policy.

candidates.label: Mathematics for economics and financial analysis
Mathematics for biological and life sciences

selection.assessment: Three complete related-fields programmes pass the evidence, coherence, course-content, pairwise distinctness and feasibility gates. The closest route integrates mathematical methods with algorithms, optimisation, probability and data models. The second uses the explicit climate direction to organise a materially different Earth-system and scientific-data curriculum. The third uses the explicit mathematics-for-economics and financial-mathematics interests to organise a quantitative economics and decision-model route. All pairwise differences exceed 30 EC. The biological/life-science and history-of-mathematics directions remain recorded but are not pursued beyond the maximum of three. None of the accepted curricula is presented as proof-intensive pure Mathematics.

blocks: Both provide programming for mathematical problem solving; UCR supplies a general Python foundation rather than mathematics-specific research programming.
Both teach introductory calculus. Utrecht teaches linear algebra alongside it.
Both study graphs and trees. UCR focuses on algorithms and data structures, while Utrecht also develops combinatorial counting and discrete proofs.
Both develop matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations; the external component also continues calculus.
Both use computational approximation for equations and integrals and assess numerical error.
Both model systems with differential equations; UCR concentrates on linear systems, transforms and state-space representations rather than the full ODE/PDE modelling course.
Both establish probability; UCR integrates probability distributions with estimation, inference and simulation.
Both develop multivariable calculus. Utrecht emphasises proofs and theoretical results in analysis.
UCR logic courses develop formal reasoning, but no selected course reproduces a dedicated proof-writing foundation.
UCR calculus does not reproduce a cumulative proof-intensive analysis course.
UCR has no abstract algebra course in groups and rings.
This later course develops proof-based multivariable analysis and prepares for differentiable manifolds.
Utrecht gives ordinary differential equations and their theory a dedicated course.
General projects and research methods do not reproduce the target’s dedicated mathematics laboratory.
These electives count toward Utrecht’s 45 EC profiling space.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC mathematics thesis. UCR’s optional 15 EC research element is separate from the scheduled courses.
The 45 EC profiling space can include an approved minor.

notes.text: Utrecht builds a sequence in mathematical proof, abstract algebra, analysis, topology and independent mathematical research. The UCR examples develop related techniques through computation and applications in science and economics.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Mathematics degree develops proofs, mathematical theory and modelling. Teaching is mainly in Dutch in the first year and shifts toward English in later years.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples focus on applied mathematics and algorithms, modelling Earth systems, or quantitative economics.
